summary.name: Music-Synchronized Animation (style-105, Motion Design and Cinematography). This is a timing discipline that schedules reveals, cuts and motion accents from measured musical events. It is layered over a separate visual style, so it is not a standalone look.
summary.visualIdentity: The explicit source defines the method, not a fixed aesthetic. The reviewed demo shows an SVG ball striking tuned bars, with each contact causing compression, a ripple ring and a note-length brighten. Night-canvas and editor-screen looks in the source review were the authors' choices, not style rules.
summary.suitableUses: Explicitly suited to music videos and lyric videos where a visual system must follow beats or sections. Combination guidance names abstract shapes for music videos and lyric words for lyric videos. Interactive HTML with a precomputed beat map and pauses is listed as an application. Explanatory or product uses are unspecified.
summary.limitations: The style requires a supporting visual style and cannot operate alone. Beats must be measured offline and manually verified; live audio analysis is prohibited during export. Source review covered only one frame per second from 1 to 8 seconds, with no audio or later scenes verified. Same-beat starts and removed reading time are avoided. The motion-040 reference is labelled Phrase Scatter, a metadata inconsistency.
summary.palette: The background policy is scene_dependent, so the swatch #F3EBDD is an illustrative example rather than a required canvas. Example tokens are foreground #293B44, accent_1 #628C98 and accent_2 #BA7B61. No approved exact colors were supplied, and task-provided colors would override these. Foreground on background measures 9.836:1, while both accents fail normal text at 3.174 and 3.379 and remain decorative only. Gradients are disabled, and color-family and count limits are unspecified beyond visual_cues.
summary.motionAndInteraction: Motion runs on one seekable GSAP timeline evaluated from composition time. Cue-driven contact-response chains, density changes and pauses before final hits are explicit in the recipe. Parts return to rest during breaks and silence. Motion references are optional: motion-037 phrase step-in, motion-038 punctuation zoom, motion-039 radial burst and motion-040 hard word cuts. Motion-012, 014 and 015 need scene support. Interaction is limited to precomputed beat-map pauses.
summary.audio: Audio is essential to the method, but genre, tempo, voice and layer choices are unspecified. The full-video route uses offline librosa beat and onset detection plus NumPy band RMS, with manually verified beats. One shared cue table drives both GSAP visuals and HyperFrames audio placement, accounting for sample attack. Silent previews use an explicitly labelled demonstration table, not analyzed sound.
summary.assetRequirements: Required assets are a task-supplied or authorized audio track, plus saved JSON analysis of beats, onsets, bands and energy. Without audio, a labelled demonstration cue table is the fallback. Motion-037 to 040 need an approved punctuation or mark asset. Local fonts and assets must be loaded before rendering. Style-105 mandates no specific artwork.
summary.combinations: Style-105 needs a visual system partner. Style-094 (abstract shapes) fits music videos: shapes divide on beats, use primary palette only and avoid same-beat starts. Style-093 (lyric words) fits lyric videos: words land on stressed beats, with reading holds and synced captions. Other styles in the motion compatibility lists are listed without detailed guidance.
summary.productionApproach: HyperFrames is the primary pipeline for composition timing, validation and export, with Remotion used only on a documented fallback. SVG is the style renderer; GSAP is the motion engine. Python librosa and NumPy run offline for cues; chroma-js validates palettes and contrast. mo.js is optional but was rejected for this recipe to avoid a second clock. Verify direct, backward and frame-level seeks.
